h.select_rule: Rank by: plausible mechanism supported by known empirical regularities (saturation, redundancy, optimization difficulty, capacity trade-offs) AND a direction most practitioners would not predict. Drop hypotheses that merely restate that removing a path increases the importance of the remaining ones.
h.strategy: Use the gap list to find interactions the literature leaves unsettled. Prefer conditional effects driven by diminishing returns: an edit's benefit shrinks when the parent already has that capability elsewhere, and a removal costs little when redundant capacity exists. Also consider optimization effects: extra parameters or depth can hurt in some contexts, while simple identity-like options can help trainability. Avoid hypotheses whose condition simply disconnects or trivializes the edited component. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields, conditions and both directions.

hyps.why: A direct skip from input to output already makes the cell trainable and supplies a baseline path, so extra conv capacity on edge 5 adds less.
The identity shortcut on edge 3 diminishes the marginal gain of a conv feeding the same output node.
A conv-rich node 2 supplies learned features that a downstream conv on edge 5 can exploit, giving complementary depth.
Removing the direct edge costs little when a conv path from node 1 to the output already provides redundant capacity.
A conv on edge 5 makes edge 3 redundant, so removing it is cheaper than when the output has few strong inputs.
Two parallel identity paths into the output are redundant, so a second skip adds little compared with when edge 3 is a conv.
A second pool feeding the output provides redundant smoothing, so adding pooling on edge 5 helps less than alongside conv siblings.
When the sibling edge into node 3 is already a strong conv, an additional conv1x1 has diminishing returns.
Node 2 already receives a conv via edge 2, so a further conv on edge 1 is partly redundant.
Skip on edge 2 adds an identity-like path to a node already fed by a conv, aiding gradient flow without redundant parameters.
